data.title: 3 out of 4 communications services stocks deliver EPS wins this week: Earnings Scorecard
data.description:
Communications services stocks grabbed the spotlight this week as Wall Street digested earnings reports from major names, including Alphabet and Verizon .

The communications services sector lost over 14% so far this year, compared to the nearly 13% rise in the broader S&P 500 Index.

In this week's earnings recap, four tickers reported results, all of which three reported earnings beats. On the revenue side, two companies exceeded revenue expectations, while two companies trailed estimates.

Below are the latest quarterly reports from some key players, which reported results this week:

Alphabet closed over 12% lower on Thursday following the tech giant’s release of the company's third-quarter financial results, which marked its first quarterly earnings miss since Q4 2022. Q3 earnings trailed Wall Street estimates, despite a more than doubling of Google Cloud revenue as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure and services surged.

Verizon Communications reported third-quarter revenue and adjusted earnings above analysts’ estimates, as well as stronger subscriber additions and higher margins that helped the telecom company lift its full-year 2026 guidance for a third consecutive quarter.

T-Mobile increased the number of new customers and saw higher average revenue per account (ARPA) leading to a 7.4% increase in third-quarter revenue and a 34% improvement in earnings, both of which beat Wall Street’s expectations.

For the upcoming week, Charter Communications , Live Nation Entertainment , Fox , and News Corp are some communication services names that are scheduled to report quarterly results.

data.title: Yes, Alphabet Stock Got Hammered. No, We're Not Selling. — Barrons.com
data.description:
The Google-parent trades at a rare discount. If it simply returns to its historical valuation relative to Apple, the stock has nearly 50% upside.

By Al Root

Weak tech earnings are sending investors for the hills, so it may not be the best time for optimism. It also isn't a time to overreact.

Shares of Google-parent Alphabet have been hammered. Yes, there are risks — as there are with any company spending big on the artificial intelligence buildout. But Barron's is sticking with its call.

The company is still an AI winner. And now shares look shockingly cheap, trading at half the multiple that AI-wary Apple fetches.

We first picked Alphabet in November 2024, when shares traded at about $168, arguing then that fears of a breakup and the death of Google search at the hands of OpenAI's ChatGPT were overblown. That advice worked out well for readers who listened. With Alphabet stock at about $320 in November 2025, we reiterated our position.

That call looked solid until AI fears reemerged over the summer. The iShares Semiconductor exchange-traded fund peaked in June after Broadcom's disappointing earnings report that included weaker-than-expected guidance for its semiconductor business. (Guidance was for 200% year-over-year growth.)

That was also about the time that Alphabet announced an $80 billion stock sale, and days before SpaceX raised $75 billion in its record-setting IPO. Questions swirled: Were tech players spending too aggressively on AI? Will they make money? How are they financing the buildout?

Fear reached a tipping point earlier this week when Alphabet reported weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings. Operating profit of almost $41 billion only grew 30% from a year ago. The problem? Wall Street was looking for $43 billion.

Shares fell almost 13% to $282.32 after earnings, pushing shares down more than 30% from the high of $404.47 reached in May. A $2 billion profit miss drove a $560 billion one-day decline in market value.

Barron's isn't here to argue with the market. But it is important to remain clear-eyed when volatility picks up. The earnings miss had little to do with AI.

Alphabet's cloud business more than doubled in the quarter, up from closer to 80% growth in the second quarter. Other cloud businesses are also seeing strong growth. Amazon.com's AWS business grew by 39% in the same quarter, faster than in the second quarter. Microsoft's Azure cloud business grew by 48% in the quarter — again — faster than in the second quarter.

And those performances came after other positive AI developments this week. AI growth at SpaceX was better than expected, and Anthropic's IPO registration statement showed relatively impressive profitability.

Alphabet's problem was that ad spending on Google search grew by 12%, down from 17% last quarter; ad spending on YouTube grew by 9%, down from 13%.

That raises two risks.

For one, it suggests that the economy isn't as strong as it once was. Results from other tech firms bear that out. Amazon.com's retail business was relatively weak in the third quarter, and Intel plunged partly because of an unexpected downturn in personal computers. Soaring memory chip prices have made them more expensive.

The economy is a risk that all investors need to continuously monitor. But it isn't the main factor that will determine Alphabet's stock direction over the coming months.

That comes down to the second risk: cannibalization. In other words, is Google's AI business eating search?

And that is where there is no shortage of opinion on Wall Street. Melius analyst Ben Reitzes called Alphabet's earnings evidence of secular decline. Most analysts skew positive, however. "AI mode [search] monetization is just beginning," Citi analyst Ronald Josey said. KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst Justin Patterson called the quarter an "air pocket," adding search monetization headwinds are "transitory." Deutsche Bank analyst Benjamin Black said AI is driving the strongest search-query growth in five years. He expects Alphabet to earn money from the search growth — eventually — likening it to when Meta Platforms first rolled out Reels, which initially took user engagement away from Facebook and Instagram's core feed.

Analyst commentary is worth considering. Valuation is a better reason to buy.

Alphabet trades for 18 times estimated earnings over the next 12 months, a discount to the S&P 500's 19 times multiple. Alphabet is the second cheapest stock of the Magnificent Seven. Nvidia shares trade at about 15 times.

Furthermore, Alphabet and Apple often trade at the same multiple, with a 25% discount being relatively normal over the past few years. Alphabet stock is now trading for less than 50% of Apple's 36-times multiple, the biggest discount between those two stocks over the past five years. If that 25% discount returned, Alphabet stock would trade at $400, up almost 50% from recent levels.

And what about Alphabet's free cash flow, which has been negative for two straight quarters? Well, Alphabet isn't a startup looking for profitability. It is spending on AI to build a new trillion-dollar business. If it shut off spending, free cash flow would return — but would investors really prefer that? Probably not.

data.title: Senegalese lawmakers reject revised budget key for new IMF deal
data.description:
Senegalese lawmakers on Friday rejected for a second time a revised budget that is crucial to sealing a new programme with the International Monetary Fund, according to a statement from the country's ruling party PASTEF.

The finance committee of Senegal's National Assembly said last Tuesday it would review the revised budget it had initially rejected.

  • PASTEF cited lack of budgetary transparency, ineffective cost-of-living measures, and the government's refusal to provide key documents or rationalise special funds as reasons for the rejection

  • The deadlock could derail Senegal's hopes of a board vote on a $2.2 billion, three-year IMF programme as early as next month

  • Senegal has been grappling with a debt burden that had reached 132% of gross domestic product by the ​end of 2024, IMF figures show, after the government discovered billions of dollars in misreported borrowing by the previous administration

  • The amended 2026 budget cuts real GDP growth to 2.7% from roughly 5% and widens the deficit to 7.6% of GDP from 5.4%

data.title: Meta is said to form bipartisan influence group ahead of elections
data.description:
Meta is building a bipartisan group of former political operatives ahead of midterm elections as the Facebook owner seeks to deepen its relationships with both Democrats and Republicans, Axios reported on Saturday.

According to sources, Meta president and vice chairman Dina Powell McCormick, a former bank executive who served the first Trump administration, is spearheading a new recruitment drive to achieve the goal.

The hiring initiative under Powell McCormick saw Michael Hacker, a longtime aide to House Democratic power broker Jim Clyburn, joining Meta as VP of compute initiatives. Also, Nick Schmit, a former top aide to the Biden Administration’s Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo, joined as director of strategic partnership management.

The company has also added several former Trump administration officials, including Pat Trueman, a senior official on Trump's 2024 presidential campaign who joined Meta's U.S. policy operation. Meanwhile, Josh Raffel, who worked with Powell McCormick during the first Trump administration, was also recently hired as VP of compute initiatives.

There was a slew of promotions aimed at facilitating the transition. While Powell McCormick recently added external affairs to her portfolio, the company promoted Brian Rice, a former aide to Democratic Secretary of State John Kerry, to lead its U.S. government affairs.

Tucker Bounds, who served on John McCain's presidential campaign, was elevated to the position of head of global communications, while C.J. Mahoney, a former Trump administration official, was named Meta's chief legal officer in January.

Mahoney, who served as deputy U.S. Trade Representative during the first Trump administration, has assumed additional policy responsibilities since then.

According to sources, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Powell McCormick met with the Democratic House Commission on Artificial Intelligence and the Innovation Economy in August following an invitation from Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.).

The discussions with Gottheimer and other Democrats who co-chair the commission focused on the company's AI strategy, including its infrastructure build-out and economic investment plans.

The meeting and the recruitments underscore Meta’s efforts to influence U.S. politics amid growing public scrutiny over artificial intelligence and data center buildout ahead of the midterm elections.

data.title: Texas brothers sentenced to 15 years in prison for armed crypto robbery, kidnapping
data.description:
Raymond Christian Garcia and Isiah Angelo Garcia, both of Waller, Texas, were sentenced to 180 months and 186 months in prison, respectively, for their armed robbery of cryptocurrency and kidnapping of a family in Grant, Minnesota.

The brothers were sentenced on Thursday before US District Judge Donovan W. Frank, according to a Friday news release. They had pleaded guilty in June.

On Sept. 19, 2025, the brothers, who had traveled from Texas to Minnesota, kidnapped Victim 1 and his family in their home at gunpoint, court documents said. They zip‑tied the family at gunpoint and held them for more than nine hours, demanding access to Victim 1’s cryptocurrency accounts.

When the brothers did not receive the amount of cryptocurrency expected, they forced Victim 1 to drive to a cabin in upstate Minnesota, where they obtained additional cryptocurrency from other devices for a total of more than $8 million.

The brothers fled after the victim’s son called 911, and police later identified and arrested them near Houston.

Brothers terrorized family at gunpoint

“Raymond and Isiah Garcia violated the sanctity of a home, abducted a victim, terrorized a family at gunpoint for hours, and disrupted an entire community in a brazen act of violence and greed,” said FBI Minneapolis Field Office Special Agent in Charge Christopher D. Dotson.

Cointelegraph reported in July that home invasions had become the most common form of crypto wrench attacks during the first half of 2026, rising to 20 publicly reported incidents from just one a year earlier, according to blockchain security firm CertiK.

CertiK said in July it verified 52 wrench attacks worldwide in the first half of 2026, up 33% from 39 incidents during the same period in 2025. Kidnappings rose to 16 from 12.

data.title: IDBI Bank employees' forum opposes Fairfax stake sale, seeks parliamentary review
data.description:
The United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees opposed the proposed sale of a majority stake in IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax, calling for an immediate suspension of the process and a comprehensive review under parliamentary scrutiny.

The forum said the decision was ill-timed and lacked adequate justification, arguing that volatile market conditions called for caution, transparent valuation and wider public deliberation.

Speaking to PTI Videos, IDBI Bank Officers Association President Surav Kumar said, "There is no reason for the sale of our bank specially to the foreign player."

IDBI Banks proposed privatisation is the culmination of a process that began after the lender ran into serious financial trouble. In May 2017, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) placed it under the Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework because of weak capital adequacy, poor asset quality and losses. Its net non-performing assets had exceeded 13% in March 2017.

In early 2019, the Life Insurance Corporation of India acquired a 51% controlling stake in IDBI, becoming its largest shareholder. The RBI subsequently classified the lender as a private-sector bank for regulatory purposes. After the banks financial position improved, the central bank lifted the PCA restrictions in March 2021, subject to conditions and continued monitoring.

On October 14, the Cabinet approved Fairfax as the strategic buyer of 60.72% of IDBI for a consideration of Rs 52,878 crore. The government has defended the valuation process, saying independent professional agencies assessed the bank using the market multiple and asset valuation methods. It has also argued that IDBIs volatile share price was not a reliable standalone benchmark.

The IDBI sale has triggered a public exchange between Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman. Gandhi has backed the banks employees and questioned why the government wants to sell a lender that has returned to profit. He contrasted the Congress-era establishment of banks with the current government's decision to sell them, and has also raised concerns about employees service conditions, pensions and the impact of privatisation on reservation policies.

Sitharaman hit back, accusing the Congress of treating banks as personal entities and pressuring them to lend to favoured business groups. She argued that politically influenced lending contributed to IDBIs earlier bad-loan problems and said the Modi government had revived the bank through recapitalisation and improved management. data.title: Wall Street braces for market volatility as Democrats eye control of Congress in US midterm elections
data.description:
Wall Street expects Democrats to win at least one of the houses of Congress in the US midterm elections on Tuesday, setting the stage for a potentially volatile ride in the stock and bond markets with artificial intelligence oversight, defense spending and crypto legislation on the table.

A UBS basket of stocks tied to Republicans has plunged since hitting a peak in August, badly lagging the S&P 500 Index. One major area where this could show up is in the AI trade that has been driving the stock market for the past few years, as Democrats are expected to push for stricter regulation and oversight of the technology. Meanwhile, local governments are under pressure to block data centers from being built in their communities.

If the “big political takeaway” from the election is that “data centers are bad, that would be impactful for growth,” said Robert Waldner, chief investment officer at Invesco Advisers Inc.

Read More: Is the AI boom cracking? Wall Street's tech sell-off raises questions over what comes next

The election arrives with the AI trade in the equity market already under scrutiny. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index tumbled 4.8% across Thursday and Friday after reports from major players raised concerns about heavy spending on AI, while Treasury yields fell as traders piled into haven assets.

Other industries could be in the crosshairs after the vote. If the Democrats push to rein in defense spending, military contractors would likely feel the pinch. Big banks that have been raking in profits on a flood of deals could face scrutiny. And firms tied to cryptocurrencies are likely to catch some Congressional heat simply based on the industry’s close ties to the Trump family.

All of which has some Wall Street pros positioning for selling pressure in stocks and demand for safer government bonds. In addition, many traders appear to be so locked into their positions and their expectations for a closely divided Congress that they’re vulnerable to volatile swings.

“Investors are heading into the election long the dollar and short duration, with little protection against volatility – particularly in equity markets,” Corpay strategist Karl Schamotta said. “The consensus expects a narrow Democratic victory to produce gridlock in Congress, leaving the president to pursue his objectives through executive action, but there are significant tail risks.”

Read More: What's fuelling the Nasdaq crash? AI spending fears, Intel rout and Anthropic debt concerns drive selloff

Here are the markets and equity sectors worth watching with just days to go before the vote.

Treasuries

History suggests Congressional gridlock is good for bonds by preventing ambitious policies that increase deficits and raise yields on longer-dated Treasuries. This time, however, bond watchers say any fiscal relief will be limited and unlikely to generate a sustained rally because the deficit, at roughly 6% of the economy, has rarely been this large outside of a recession.

“We have way too much debt that will be reckoned with at some point,” said Oliver Chambers, head of fixed income SMA at Clark Capital Management. “But if for the next two years, gridlock means we don’t add to it at the same rate we’ve been adding to it, I think that’s a good thing.”

A particularly strong showing by Democrats could lead to lower Treasury yields if investors see it as a sign of Americans’ appetite for AI regulation, which would pressure tech stocks and dent expectations for economic growth.

The Dollar

Like Treasuries, the dollar could get a boost from a Democratic victory based on the same anticipated stabilizing effect of a split Congress.

Some investors believe a divided government could lead President Donald Trump to lean on policies he can implement unilaterally through executive power. Any escalation with Iran, which Trump has suggested may come after the election, is expected to continue supporting the dollar by driving up energy prices and pushing the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates. New tariffs could also support the US currency by stoking inflation — unless they spark a global “sell America” trade like the one that became popular last year.

Technology and AI Infrastructure

Regardless of what happens in the midterms, Trump will still be president and is likely to veto any legislation that’s considered unfavorable to the technology industry. That may limit risk for chipmaker Nvidia Corp. and the major AI spenders like Alphabet Inc., Meta Platforms Inc. and Microsoft Corp. Still, strategists are bracing for Democratic outperformance to hurt sentiment around the AI trade.

“The midterms will be critical not for the immediate risk of federal policy restricting data centers but to lay the groundwork for potential legislation toward that end in 2029,” said Ariana Salvatore, head of US public policy research at Morgan Stanley.

Data center real estate investment trusts and neocloud companies are exposed to proposals for a tax on computing power, according to Morgan Stanley analysts. On the other hand, off-the-grid power providers like Bloom Energy Corp., Cummins Inc. and GE Vernova Inc. may get a boost from more restrictive policies, the analysts wrote.

Healthcare

Hospitals may benefit if Democrats manage to walk back Medicaid cuts included in last year’s tax bill, said Tobin Marcus, head of US policy and politics at Wolfe Research. Democrats looking for concessions in a possible debt ceiling negotiation may seek wins in healthcare, he said.

Hospital names like Acadia Healthcare Co., HCA Healthcare Inc. and Tenet Healthcare Corp. have near-term upside linked to the election, according to Jefferies analysts. Insurers Centene Corp. and Oscar Health Inc. also could catch bids on hopes that Democrats will negotiate to restore enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies that expired at the end of last year, though the firm considers that outcome unlikely.

Defense

Shares of defense contractors have underperformed this year amid worries that a potential Democratic sweep would lead to tighter oversight and funding delays. Drone stocks such as AeroVironment Inc. and Kratos Defense & Security Solutions Inc. have had some of the biggest declines. If the Democrats take control of one or both chambers, funding that’s critical for the Pentagon’s ambitious drone production plans may be in jeopardy.

If Republicans hold their ground, however, military spending could rise, according to JPMorgan, which points to L3Harris Technologies Inc., Lockheed Martin Corp. and Northrop Grumman Corp. as possible beneficiaries.

Financials and Crypto

Republicans tend to favor lighter oversight of the financial sector, so a surprise sweep by the party would favor lenders such as Bank of America Corp., Citigroup Inc. and Wells Fargo & Co., according to JPMorgan.

However, the election is unlikely to alter issues like bank stress testing, since the heads of the Fed, Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. and Office of the Comptroller of the Currency are likely to remain in place for several years, Barclays analyst Jason Goldberg said.

In cryptocurrencies, the odds for any legislation supporting the industry may decline if Democrats take control. Democrats, along with a few Republicans, blocked the Clarity Act in September, sending stocks such as Coinbase Global Inc. and Circle Internet Group Inc. tumbling.

Potential Investigation Targets

Wall Street is bracing for Democrats to launch a range of investigations. Hearings focused on AI could create market risk, according to Evercore ISI, and companies like Nvidia and Amazon.com Inc. have already been hit with investigative inquiries from Democrats. Evercore also expects probes into industries tied to affordability issues, such as energy, healthcare, food production and agriculture.

Companies that have received equity investments from the US government, like Intel Corp., International Business Machines Corp. and rare earth producer MP Materials Corp. could also face inquiries, creating risk to their shares.

Elon Musk’s Empire

The Democrats winning one or both houses of Congress could have implications for major Republican donor Elon Musk’s companies — Tesla Inc. and SpaceX — as investors are anticipating a possible merger of the two. Though Congress can’t single-handedly kill a deal, empowered Democrats would be able to slow it down, according to First New York’s Vikram Rai.

“Both of these stocks have major headline risk if we get a blue sweep,” he said.

data.title: Chainalysis says hacker using ‘offensive agentic techniques’ accessed its customers’ names and emails
data.description:
Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said an unidentified hacker using "offensive agentic techniques" broke into its systems and internal tools this month and accessed some "non-sensitive" customer data, according to a notice sent to affected customers.

Chainalysis published the full text of the notice in a blog post on Friday evening. The attacker accessed "some non-sensitive customer data, such as user IDs, full names, email addresses, and organization role labels for users provisioned on our platform," the company said, pledging to send a follow-up to each client detailing which exact information was accessed.

"Based on the evidence available to date, we have found no indication that these incidents resulted in the unauthorized access of investigation content (such as graphs, notes, or cases), transaction or query results, passwords in clear text, MFA secrets, or user session tokens," Chainalysis wrote.

Chainalysis did not say when it detected the intrusion, which was first flagged by International Cyber Digest, how many customers were affected, which specific vulnerabilities the attacker exploited, or how AI agents played a role in the breach. The Block has reached out to Chainalysis for further details.

Chainalysis said it has contracted third-party cybersecurity experts and is using large language models to support a broad security review of its platform. The firm advised affected firms to turn on two-factor authentication and to be on the lookout for suspicious activities like unexpected password reset requests or authentication prompts.

Chainalysis breach "not related" to Binance hack

Chainalysis said the incident is "not related to the recent crypto theft at Binance." Chainalysis, Elliptic and TRM have each attributed the roughly $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korean hacking groups, which, according to Binance, managed to compromise an engineer's laptop and access a service container. The exchange's co-CEO Richard Teng said the breach was more complex than the compromise of a single employee's permissions, though.

On Ethereum, the attacker used EIP-7702 to turn a Binance hot wallet into a sweeper, The Block previously reported. The sweeper contract was only around 130 lines, Immunefi Vice President Simone Imbrescia said in a statement shared with The Block. "The hard part sometimes is getting access to a system powerful enough to make very simple code devastating," Imbrescia said.

Chainalysis, which puts the theft at $6.4 billion, has continued to track the stolen funds. On Friday, the firm said it was seeing "never-seen-before laundering patterns," with thousands of transactions in a short period suggesting the attackers were using automation to obscure the trail. Rather than simply forwarding funds to new addresses, the attackers repeatedly circulated the stolen crypto among addresses, often sending funds back to addresses used earlier in the sequence, the firm said, sharing a diagram showing the funds' movements.

On Saturday, Chainalysis said the exploiters have used DeFi lending protocols on the Tron network to stay ahead of stablecoin freezes since the early hours of the attack. The hackers swapped Tron's native TRX token for various stablecoins and deposited them in a lending protocol, identified by onchain analysts Specter and Ian Unsworth as JustLend, in exchange for receipt tokens, which cannot be frozen by stablecoin issuers. The attackers then moved those receipts to clean wallets, redeemed them for stablecoins and bridged the funds off Tron, swapping them for ETH on the other side, according to the firm.

"Now the exploiter is free of worry of a freeze," the firm wrote. Chainalysis' Saturday thread noted that around $2.8 billion in stablecoins have already been frozen by stablecoin firms such as Circle and Tether. "Of course, exchanging stablecoins for ETH does not make the hackers bulletproof," Chainalysis added.

data.title: Shyam Metalics Q2 Profit Jumps 88%, Plans Rs 360 Cr Coal Block Investment
data.description:
Consolidated revenue rises 33 per cent to Rs 5,960 crore in the September quarter as the company proposes a 51 per cent stake in the entity holding rights to Chhattisgarh’s Phutamura coal block

Shyam Metalics and Energy reported an 88.4 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit attributable to owners of the parent company at Rs 493.35 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, compared with Rs 261.76 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Consolidated revenue from operations increased 33.4 per cent to Rs 5,960.19 crore during the second quarter of FY27, against Rs 4,467.40 crore a year earlier. Total income rose to Rs 5,994.34 crore from Rs 4,536.53 crore, according to the company's unaudited financial results approved by the board on 31 October.

Consolidated profit after tax stood at Rs 510.99 crore, of which Rs 493.35 crore was attributable to owners of the parent company and Rs 17.64 crore to non-controlling interests. Earnings per share increased to Rs 18.36 from Rs 9.36 in the year-ago quarter. For the six months ended 30 September 2026, consolidated revenue from operations stood at Rs 11,415.28 crore, compared with Rs 8,890.39 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Coal Block Acquisition Plan

Alongside the quarterly results, the board approved a proposal to acquire a 51 per cent controlling equity stake in Alom Solar, the entity that holds the mining rights for the Phutamura coal block in Raigarh district, Chhattisgarh.

The coal block covers approximately 7.324 sq km and has estimated reserves of around 170 million tonnes. Shyam Metalics said the proposed acquisition would support strategic backward integration by securing long-term coal supplies for captive power generation and its steel manufacturing operations.

The transaction is subject to execution of definitive agreements and necessary statutory approvals. Alom Solar will become a subsidiary of Shyam Metalics upon completion of the acquisition. The company has indicated a completion timeline of on or before 30 November 2026.

The board has also proposed an initial capital expenditure of approximately Rs 360 crore for the development and operationalisation of the Phutamura coal block. Shyam Metalics' proposed 51 per cent contribution to the initial capital expenditure is approximately Rs 183.60 crore, while the remaining 49 per cent will be funded by its joint venture partner.

data.title: Chinese Executive Close to Nvidia CEO Suspected of Giving China Information — WSJ
data.description:
By Amrith Ramkumar, Lingling Wei and Robbie Whelan

Officials in the U.S., Singapore and Taiwan have grown concerned that a data-center industry executive with close ties to Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang is a Chinese intelligence source, according to people familiar with the matter, potentially giving Beijing access to information about the world's most valuable artificial-intelligence chips.

U.S. officials last year concluded that Chinese citizen Alice Huang, then a top executive at Megaspeed International, was sharing information with the Chinese government while working with Nvidia to build data centers in Asia, the people said. Huang, who also goes by Huang Le, isn't related to the Nvidia CEO.

Authorities in Singapore, where Megaspeed is based, and in Taiwan had separately investigated Alice Huang's ties to China, at one point putting physical surveillance teams on her, some of the people said. Officials involved in those investigations suspected she was recruited by Chinese intelligence services after they learned of what they saw as a close relationship between her and the Nvidia chief, the people said.

In late 2024, as authorities started to surveil her, Alice Huang disappeared into China for a period, the people said. It couldn't be determined where she is now or whether she still holds a top role at Megaspeed. Attempts to reach her for comment were unsuccessful.

Megaspeed didn't respond to requests for comment.

The Chinese Embassy in Washington rejected the allegations, saying that China opposes what it called the peddling of a "Chinese spy narrative" and that its technological development is grounded in "independent innovation."

"We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know," an Nvidia spokesman said, adding that Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang "are not unusual or unexpected" given their business ties.

A representative of the Singapore Police Force said investigations into Megaspeed were ongoing and declined to give specifics. "While we do not enforce unilateral export controls imposed by other countries, we act firmly against companies and individuals who violate our laws and are engaged in fraudulent and dishonest practices," the representative said.

After this story was published, Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said in an additional statement that "there were no such investigations conducted in respect of Alice Huang" for her alleged ties to China.

Taiwan's representative office in Washington said it doesn't comment on specific intelligence or security matters.

Nvidia's technology is considered one of the most prized American technology assets, making Huang a global superstar and helping him form a close relationship with President Trump. With Huang's encouragement, Trump has enacted industry-friendly chip and AI policies and even approved some sales of older Nvidia chips to China while negotiating with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Huang is often caught between the world's two leading economies, seeking to keep them both hooked on the chips powering leading AI models.

In late 2024, Commerce Department officials began investigating whether Megaspeed was diverting Nvidia's chips to China, circumventing U.S. export controls meant to protect critical technologies. That investigation largely stalled, according to people familiar with the matter. The Justice Department is now leading the probe into Megaspeed.

Many U.S. security experts are worried that companies are skirting rules preventing advanced chips from going to China, often by building data centers in nearby countries and then letting Chinese companies access that computing capacity remotely. The analysts have criticized what they describe as the Trump administration's unwillingness to close what they call loopholes.

"When you look at the actual behavior of federal agencies, there's little to no evidence that they are willing to take the meaningful actions that are required to catch smugglers, deter smuggling and hold companies accountable," said Greg Allen, chief executive of a research firm focused on chips and geopolitics.

Late last year, Megaspeed said it had undergone several government reviews into allegations of chip diversions. "These thorough investigations have confirmed that there has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company," Megaspeed said in a statement at the time.

The investigation and concerns about Megaspeed were previously reported by the New York Times.

Officials in the Biden administration opened the initial investigation into Megaspeed amid a broader effort to restrict the flow of U.S. chips to much of the world. The Biden team's efforts were criticized by Huang and others in the industry, who called it government overreach that would hurt a leading U.S. sector.

Despite its dominance in the West, Nvidia has been largely locked out of China since last April, when the Commerce Department banned sales of its powerful Hopper generation of processors, including a chip with degraded capabilities that was specially designed for the Chinese market. China sales accounted for about one-fifth of Nvidia's revenue in 2023, but since the U.S. government tightened restrictions, that revenue has vanished.

This has been a sore point for Huang, the Nvidia CEO, who has said that he believes roughly half of the world's best AI developers are based in China and should be using Nvidia's hardware to build products.

"We went from 95% market share to 0% [in China], and so I can't imagine any policymaker thinking that that's a good idea, that whatever policy we implemented caused America to lose one of the largest markets in the world," Huang said last year at an event hosted by securities firm Citadel.

Megaspeed and companies like it buy Nvidia chips with the goal of installing them in data centers in countries such as Malaysia, then selling that computing capacity to tech giants and other customers. The Singapore-based company was set up in 2023 after a Chinese firm split off its overseas operation.

Alice Huang was one of its top executives and was photographed in public with Jensen Huang in Taipei in 2024 and 2025. The photos were taken at meetings that included other Nvidia cloud partners in Asia, the Nvidia spokesman said.

After Trump began his second term, Jensen Huang repeatedly asked the president and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to give Nvidia expanded access to the Chinese market and loosen strict restrictions limiting the flow of U.S. chips. Lutnick's agency rolled back many of the Biden administration's regulations on chip exports.

The industry-friendly approach has frustrated some in the administration who think the White House is being too deferential to China while trade talks continue. Beijing's own push for technological self-reliance has also cut into Nvidia's sales of lower-end chips there.

In March, Nvidia was dragged into another scandal involving China when Wally Liaw, the co-founder of server maker Super Micro, was arrested on charges of violating U.S. export-control laws by allegedly helping smuggle $2.5 billion worth of servers containing advanced Nvidia microchips into China. Super Micro said at the time that it was cooperating with federal investigators, and Nvidia said compliance with export restrictions is a top priority. Both companies denied wrongdoing at the time, and Liaw's attorneys couldn't be reached for comment. Liaw pleaded not guilty to the charges.

data.title: Do Security Cameras Make Us Feel Safer or Give Us Unnecessary Frights? — WSJ
data.description:
By Julie Jargon

Amanda Presswood was in her upstairs bedroom last month when she checked her Ring doorbell camera to see if it was raining. It was dry out. She watched as two cars drove down the quiet street beyond her porch.

Then she heard voices.

The first was a male voice, followed by women's voices. The speech was garbled, but to Presswood it sounded like the male voice asked, "Can I talk to you?" There was nobody on camera.

Presswood lives with her adult son in a 93-year-old house in Galesburg, Ill., a small town not far from the Iowa border. The school-bus attendant had been spooked by unsettling anomalies before — footsteps when no one's around, the TV suddenly powering on — but she figured there was a reasonable explanation for this incident.

"I've watched those paranormal shows and a lot of the stories can be debunked, so I tried to debunk it," she says.

Her son wasn't home. Presswood knew her neighbors weren't home either, and that no one was at the church across the street. She panned around with the camera and didn't see anyone. She went outside but there was no sign of anyone.

So far, her ghostly story remains a mystery.

Home-security cameras are meant to reduce the anxiety we feel from the unknown: Who's at the door? How is the baby sleeping? What's happening at home when we're on vacation? And these cameras do provide solace, occasionally serving to prevent problematic behavior and even criminal acts.

There are cases, however, when the video feed only fuels our worries. And in rare instances, what we see can be inexplicable — or downright terrifying.

Christine Peck, owner of the Sock Monkey Kids Shop in Cape May County, N.J., received a motion alert from the store's Ring camera one day in August 2024. The shop was closed. She figured an employee had left something and had gone in to retrieve it, but no one was inside.

Instead, she saw a black shadowy mist drifting around the room filled with toys.

Mysterious things have happened at the shop before. Several times plush toys have fallen off shelves with seemingly no intervention. The wispy apparition was the last straw. She turned off the camera alerts.

"I don't look anymore," she says. "I don't want to know."

Peck's area actually made this year's list of spookiest cities in America: Cape May was ranked sixth by home-security company Vivint. The company creates its ranking based on reported ghost sightings and haunted locations, among other criteria.

Ken Weeks would concur. Two years ago, he was at his winter home in Sanford, Fla., when he got a door alert from the Samsung refrigerator in his house in Cape May. Sure enough, on his Ring camera, he could see the door open slowly on its own. He even heard the ding the fridge makes when someone waves their hand under the door sensor to open it. He got chills.

Weeks asked a neighbor to check the house. Nobody was there, and there was no sign of entry.

"Being a skeptic, my first reaction was that it was a technical glitch," says Weeks, who works for a software company. "But we haven't been able to come up with a rational explanation for how that happened."

The door hasn't spontaneously opened again — though some people have complained on Reddit about the same model opening randomly. Samsung didn't respond to requests for comment.

Not all unexplained occurrences are unwelcome.

Emily Pendergast, an actress in Los Angeles, had set up a SimpliSafe indoor camera with her husband in the spring of 2024 so they could keep tabs on their new rescue pit-bull-mix puppy, Winter.

One day, while out grocery shopping, they got a motion alert. Her husband pulled out his phone.

"He stopped dead in his tracks," Pendergast recalls.

For a moment, they saw what appeared to be Lang, the beloved rescue shepherd mix they had had for nearly 13 years. Only Lang died in 2023.

Pendergast held on to the video and watched it over and over again. Earlier this month, she decided to post it on Instagram because she felt it might bring comfort to others who have lost pets. The video garnered more than seven million views. Pendergast likes to think Lang is watching over Winter.

"I felt we were able to see something we weren't intended to see," Pendergast says.

data.title: The stock market's front-runners stumbled in October. Here's where the smart money is moving now.
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis

Investors are shifting money into stocks with defensive and high-quality characteristics

Investors were spooked by the tech selloff in October.

U.S. stocks saw a strong reversal in fortunes in October, as worries about dwindling free cash flows and rising borrowing costs threw a wrench into the artificial-intelligence trade.

Tech stocks were punished, with the S&P 500's information-technology sector XX:SP500.45 snapping back-to-back monthly gains to drop 6.8% for its worst month since March 2025, FactSet data showed. Investors - spooked by fears that companies may not deliver the payoff they had expected from AI despite continuing to pour money into building data centers - leaned into traditionally more defensive parts of the equities market. They're also eyeing high-quality stocks to help mitigate sudden tech blows.

Friday's clobbering of the Invesco S&P 500 Momentum ETF SPMO, which tracks stocks in the U.S. large-cap equities index that have a high momentum score and whose portfolio is heavily weighted toward tech, left the exchange-traded fund with a 10.1% loss in October. The iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor ETF MTUM, which seeks to capture market trends by investing in U.S. stocks with strong recent performance, booked a similar drop of 10.5% in October, according to FactSet data.

"We're buying quality," said Jeff Buchbinder, chief equity strategist at LPL Financial, in a phone interview. "When you buy quality products, you are getting a little bit of a value tilt, and you're getting a little bit of underweight to the AI trade, particularly to the lower-quality segment of the AI trade."

Marta Norton, Empower's chief investment strategist, also pointed to stocks with quality characteristics as desirable in the current environment, citing their "lower levels of debt, consistent earnings streams and a measure of growth embedded in the revenue profile."

While tech's struggles in October dragged the S&P 500 SPX and Nasdaq Composite Index COMP into the red, high-quality stocks generally appeared to hold up amid the AI-related carnage.

Take the iShares MSCI USA Quality Factor ETF QUAL, which aims to invest in U.S. stocks with stable earnings and low debt. The fund ended October with a slight 0.1% gain, according to FactSet data. By contrast, the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 5.3% in October, cementing its worst monthly performance since March 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

As the AI trade's recent comeback violently reversed in October, investors have sought shelter in Treasury bonds while also taking cover in traditionally defensive stock-market sectors, like healthcare XX:SP500.35, utilities XX:SP500.55 and consumer staples XX:SP500.30.

The State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF XLP, the State Street Utilities Select Sector SPDR ETF XLU and the State Street Health Care Select Sector SPDR ETF XLV all saw enormous rallies in October.

The consumer staples ETF, whose top three holdings as of Thursday included Walmart (WMT), Costco Wholesale (COST) and Procter & Gamble Co. (PG), soared 10.9% in October. That huge gain left the State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF with its largest monthly gain ever since it began trading in 1998, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

While consumers still appear to be spending despite sticky inflation, purchases of discretionary items risk falling off if the stock market experiences a big drawdown that makes investors worried about a drop in their wealth, Russell Price, chief economist at Ameriprise Financial, told MarketWatch by phone. But consumer staples tend to fare relatively well when the economy slows, as people continue to shop for items like soap, toothpaste and shampoo.

Consumer staples tend to be "a safer place to be within the equity market," said Empower's Norton, "as there's just not a whole lot of earnings volatility there." But she cautioned that, at this point, the consumer-staples sector appears "overvalued" following its recent surge.

The S&P 500's consumer-staples sector has gained almost 16% this year after its October spike, according to FactSet data.

Still, the index's tech sector has seen an even bigger gain so far in 2026 - around 19% - despite fears over the AI trade as chip stocks sold off in October.

The PHLX Semiconductor Index SOX plunged more than 15% in October, with Intel's shares (INTC) plummeting 28.6% on Friday alone after the company's quarterly earnings report disappointed investors.

Big Tech stocks also fell Friday, as investors digested Amazon.com's (AMZN) quarterly earning results. The Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF MAGS - whose holdings include seven Big Tech stocks including Amazon, Nvidia (NVDA), Google parent Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT), Facebook parent Meta Platforms (META) and Tesla (TSLA) - dropped 4.5% in October, according to FactSet.

Hyperscalers in that group are at the center of "the AI storm." But they have appreciated by less than hot chip stocks, making them less vulnerable to a pullback, according to Norton.

The market seems to be "calling the wrestling match after the first takedown instead of waiting to see how it plays out over time," she said. "I don't think we know who the winners and losers are because we don't know exactly how customers and enterprises are going to change their behavior and interact with AI."

While the U.S. equities market's stumble in October was largely triggered by a selloff in the technology sector and Big Tech due to AI anxiety, an equal-weight version of the S&P 500 pulled off a gain as the average stock appeared to do well week after week.

The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP rallied almost 5% in October, ending Friday with a fourth straight week of gains, according to FactSet data. By contrast, the S&P 500 booked a monthly loss of 0.9%, falling for a third straight week to reduce its 2026 gain to 10.7%, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

-Christine Idzelis

data.title: Next Technology Holding may sell $450M in Bitcoin after Binance hack
data.description:
A Nasdaq-listed company valued at roughly $8 million says it may part with Bitcoin worth about $450 million. That is a stock trading for a sliver of the coins it claims to hold.

Next Technology Holding Inc. (NASDAQ: NXTT) says its board has authorized selling or borrowing against its entire stash of 5,833 BTC. The trigger was the security breach at Binance, which pushed the board to rethink the risks of holding crypto at all.

According to the deep research findings, the board approval took effect on October 30, 2026. It came one day after Binance reported a hot wallet incident on October 29 that compromised approximately $6.3 billion.

A hot wallet is the exchange equivalent of a cash register. It stays connected to the internet for fast withdrawals, which also makes it the most tempting target in the building.

Binance linked the incident to North Korean actors. Approximately $3 billion of the stolen assets have reportedly been frozen through cooperation with issuers and partners.

NXTT's resolution covers two paths. The company can sell the Bitcoin outright, or it can pledge the coins as collateral for loans.

The board handed the CEO authority over timing and method. The stated goals are to reduce market exposure and improve liquidity.

The holdings are valued at approximately $450-480 million, depending on the Bitcoin price used. The company's market capitalization sits at roughly $7-8 million.

NXTT says none of its Bitcoin is held through Binance. So the exchange breach did not directly touch its coins, at least by the company's account.

The board instead pointed to broader worries about exchange security. It also cited quantum computing, a longer-range concern for anyone holding digital assets.

The more pressing issue for investors may be verification. NXTT's filings do not name its institutional custodians, and they provide no wallet addresses that would let outsiders confirm the coins on-chain.

Without that disclosure, shareholders are working on trust. Telling investors your coins are safe while declining to show where they sit is a bit like a magician insisting the rabbit is definitely in the hat.

The company first disclosed Bitcoin purchases in 2023. It then ramped up its holdings significantly through 2024 and 2025, funding the buys through capital raises.

Per the research findings, NXTT acquired its 5,833 BTC at an average cost basis of approximately $30,000 to $31,386 per coin. That puts the total outlay at around $175-183 million.

If those figures hold, the position carries a large paper gain against its current valuation of approximately $450-480 million. Selling would lock in that gain rather than leaving it exposed to price swings.

NXTT has not bought additional Bitcoin since mid-2025. So the stash has been sitting static for some time before this week's decision.

For NXTT shareholders, the central puzzle is the valuation gap. The market is pricing the company at a tiny fraction of the Bitcoin it reports owning.

The lack of custodian names and wallet addresses likely feeds that skepticism. If NXTT sells or borrows against the coins, investors will want to see where the proceeds go.

For the Bitcoin market, a 5,833 BTC sale is meaningful but not enormous. The CEO controls timing and method, so a staggered sale or a loan structure could soften any impact.

The pledge option deserves attention too. Borrowing against Bitcoin keeps the coins on the books but adds leverage, which introduces liquidation risk if prices fall sharply.

data.title: Alphabet’s record plunge, Intel’s 30% collapse: tech’s brutal week of reckoning
data.description:
A broad selloff in technology stocks gathered pace this week, with chipmakers, cloud computing groups, cybersecurity companies and software providers all sharply lower. Several of the sector’s biggest names lost billions of dollars in market value after reporting earnings or issuing forecasts that disappointed investors

The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF fell 5.52% for the week, while the Dow Jones U.S. Software Index lost more than 3%. The Nasdaq Composite declined 1.95%, as of mid-day Friday.

Star analyst Dan Ives described the week as “absolutely brutal” for technology investors, saying the disruption from AI was becoming increasingly visible in corporate earnings.

Alphabet suffered its biggest one-day percentage decline on record on Thursday, falling as much as 13% and wiping out roughly $500B in market value. Google reported a rare earnings miss on slower growth in search advertising and a sharp increase in AI spending.

Intel shares plunged about 30% on Friday after the chipmaker issued a fourth-quarter forecast well below Wall Street expectations, warning that weakness in the personal computer market could persist through the first half of 2027.

INTC decline also dragged down semiconductor stocks. The PHLX Semiconductor Sector index fell 9%. AMD dropped 11%, Broadcom and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing each fell 6%, and Micron and Nvidia each lost 5%. SanDisk shares fell 12% on Friday despite reporting better-than-expected quarterly results and issuing stronger guidance and an eight-for-one stock split.

Amazon shares shed roughly 7% following its earnings report, as its aggressive investment plans overshadowed growth in its cloud computing business. Microsoft offered a relative bright spot, with shares down about just 2% since its results. Though it moved to raise $25B through a bond offering.

ServiceNow shares tumbled more than 25% on Thursday after the enterprise software company issued a weaker-than-expected forecast for subscription growth, reviving concerns about the potential impact of AI on traditional software businesses.

Fortinet shares plunged about 27%. Although the company beat third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, investors were disappointed by slower product revenue growth and a reduction in its full-year services revenue outlook.

Selloff spread to other software and cybersecurity companies, with Zscaler falling 7.5%, Okta losing 7.1%, Rubrik declining 5.3%, Palo Alto Networks dropping 5%, Cloudflare shedding 4.9%, CrowdStrike falling 4.6% and SentinelOne losing 3.5%, since Thursday. Twilio shares tumbled 19% on Friday despite the company beating third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates, but analysts called its smaller-than-expected beat.

The tech sell-off represented a moment for long thought rather than a full market reckoning, according to Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James.

"This pivotal tech earnings week has been a tale of two cities for tech investors…bringing a painful week to the tech bulls although the underlying drivers of the AI Revolution are even more defined going forward in our view," Ives said.

data.title: US President Trump Says Binance Claims To Have Hack 'Pretty Much Under Control,' But Warns Digital Money Has Always Been ‘A Little Bit Dangerous’
data.description:
Key points:
  • President Trump said on Friday his administration was “looking at” the Binance hack.
  • Trump acknowledged that Binance has “it pretty much under control.”
  • He said he has always felt digital money was “a little bit dangerous” because “people never see the money anymore.”

President Donald Trump said that Binance (BNB) told officials it had the fallout from its multibillion-dollar hack “pretty much under control,” while saying that he long felt that digital money was “a little bit dangerous.”

Speaking at the White House on Friday, Trump was asked whether the hack should be tied to a North Korean hacker group. “We’re looking at that,” he said. Trump added that Binance had pledged to make users whole. “They say they’re going to get it back. They’re saying they’re guaranteeing it or something,” he said.

He then pointed to the risks. He compared crypto with traditional payments, such as signing a check. “People never see the money anymore,” he said, adding that he had always felt it was “a little bit dangerous.” Still, he said, “they say they have it pretty much under control.”

Trump also told reporters in the Oval Office that authorities are not sure if North Korea was behind it, but said officials are investigating.

Despite the hack, Binance Coin’s price, the native token of BNB Chain, traded relatively flat over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BNB moved to ‘bearish’ from ‘bullish’ zones, while chatter around it stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

What Happened

Binance was hit by a hack on Thursday, with losses reported over $6 billion. Blockchain investigators ZachXBT, Blockaid and TRM Labs had said North Korea was likely behind the attack. The exchange said it had reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover users’ losses. It is also working to recover about $3 billion in frozen assets.

Why North Korean Hackers Are Different From Others

TRM Lab’s Global Head of Policy Ari Redbord said on the Bankless podcast that North Korean hackers " don't really care if [they] lose some [money] here or there." Redbord added that “They lost a lot last night, but they also made off with, arguably, what would in and of itself be the largest hack ever by 2x, right?”. According to him the hackers “care a lot less about getting caught because no one's going to jail. There's never going to be an extradition, and there's likely not going to be a criminal prosecution of any kind.”

The breach rattled crypto markets, as more than $1.6 billion in leveraged bets were wiped out, and Bitcoin (BTC) fell to a six-week low near $77,300. Following this, the CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said that “the blockchain gives us a very good shot” at tracking the stolen funds.

Not Binance’s First Breach

Binance has been hit by major attacks before, when in October 2022, an attacker exploited a bridge on BNB Chain and minted about 2 million BNB, worth roughly $570 million at the time. Then in May 2019, hackers stole about 7,000 Bitcoin, then worth roughly $40 million, from the exchange’s hot wallet. Binance covered the losses from its emergency fund.

At more than $6 billion, Thursday’s hack is the largest hacks on the chain, followed by ByBit hack, where $1.5 billion worth of Ethereum (ETH) was stolen by North Korea’s Lazarus Group.

data.title: Poland's president accuses Tusk of forced takeover of country's top court
data.description:
Polish President Karol Nawrocki on Saturday accused Prime Minister Donald Tusk of staging a forced takeover of the country's top court after the head of the court, an ally of the previous far right government, was suspended.

Late on Friday, the Constitutional Tribunal said its longest-serving judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska had suspended Bogdan Swieczkowski, the tribunal's president and an appointee of Tusk's hard-right predecessor, and was now in charge of the court.

The move escalated a battle between Nawrocki, an ally of the previous nationalist government, and Prime Minister Donald Tusk's pro-European government over control of the judiciary.

"Tonight, there was a breach of public order in the Republic of Poland and a forcible takeover of a constitutional body," Nawrocki said in a statement read by an aide outside the court early on Saturday, after the president had turned back mid-flight from a trip to Africa to address the situation.

He headed straight to the court where riot police were out in force as several hundred protesters demanded Swieczkowski's reinstatement.

Nawrocki called for urgent political consultations.

Tusk, writing on X, said his government was seeking to restore the rule of law, which the European Union had accused his predecessors — the Law and Justice Party — of subverting.

"This process is difficult, at times even painful, and requires decisive action. There is no other way," he said.

LONG-RUNNING POLITICAL DISPUTE

A long-running political dispute over the Constitutional Tribunal has effectively paralysed the institution, with the pro-European government and the nationalist president refusing to recognise appointees put forward by the other side.

The dispute dates back to 2015, when the Law and Justice sought to appoint judges to seats already filled by the previous government.

Its nominees gained a majority on the Constitutional Tribunal, while critics at home and abroad said the court no longer met the standards of an independent and impartial tribunal established by law.

After Tusk's coalition took office in 2023 it pledged to restore the rule of law and reform the court, but Law and Justice ally Nawrocki has acted to thwart those efforts since his election as president in 2025.

Earlier this year, Nawrocki refused to swear in three of six judges nominated by parliament, while Swieczkowski, a former deputy justice minister in the Law and Justice administration, declined to seat judges elected by the current parliamentary majority.

Last month, parliament appointed Tusk ally Maciej Berek to the tribunal, which critics said undermined the government's stated goal of restoring checks and balances.

data.title: Mukesh Ambani stocks: Reliance Industries vs Jio Platforms shares compared - RIL or JPL? What to buy? Experts' views
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 31 -- Mukesh Ambani stocks | Reliance Industries vs Jio Platforms shares: The two Mukesh Ambani-led companies, Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) and Jio Platforms Ltd (JPL), declared their respective Q2 Results 2026 on Friday. Both companies delivered promising Q2 numbers: RIL reported improved margins in its oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business, while JPL posted strong EBITDA margins, cash reserves, and a rise in ARPU.

According to stock market experts, both Mukesh Ambani-owned stocks are expected to open gap-up on Monday. However, they said that the situation might become tricky for those investors, who want to buy either of these two Mukesh Ambani's stocks.

Decoding Reliance Industries' Q2 Results 2026, Avinash Gorakshkar, Founder of Avinash Mentor Research, said, "Reliance Industries reported strong YoY growth during the July to September 2026 quarter on the consolidated revenue, EBITDA, and net profit front. This could become possible due to the massive recovery in the Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C) EBITDA, which grew about 70% YoY to around Rs.25,200 crore during the September 2026 quarter."

Gorakshkar said that O2C recovery is expected to continue in the next quarter as well, and hence the market is estimating strong Q3 results 2026 from Reliance Industries.

During the July to September 2026 quarter, Reliance's consolidated revenue grew 27.80% YoY to Rs.3,62,268 crore, EBITDA grew 23.9% YoY to Rs.62,409 crore, and the Profit After Tax (PAT) or net profit shot up 33.80% YoY to Rs.29,550 crore.

Speaking on Jio Platforms Q2 Results 2026, Avinash Gorakshkar said, "Like RIL, JPL too posted strong YoY growth in consolidated revenue, EBITDA and net profit. This could become possible on subscriber additions pushing the total user base to 542.4 million (including 300 million 5G users and 30 million fixed-broadband homes), with Average Revenue Per User (ARPU) climbing to Rs.218.8."

Gorakshkar said that Jio Platforms' net debt also came down to Rs.8,800 crore, which is expected to shrink or may become zero after the huge success of Rs.30,200 crore IPO launch. The IPO was a completely fresh issue, and the net proceeds have gone directly into the company's balance sheet.

Jio Platforms' consolidated revenue grew 11.30% YoY to Rs.47,485 crore, net profit went up 16.60% YoY to Rs.21,879 crore, while the company's margins expanded 250 bps to 54.10%.

Comparing the Q2 Results 2026 of these two Mukesh Ambani-owned stocks, Avinash Gorakshkar said, "Both RIL and JPL delivered strong Q2 FY27 numbers following JPL's Rs.30,188-crore IPO and market debut on October 28, 2026. Deciding between them depends on whether you prefer a diversified conglomerate play with a holding company discount or a pure-play digital and telecom growth stock."

Mahesh M Ojha, VP - Research and Business Development at KC Securities, said, "If someone wants to play the theme, then JPL is a suitable choice for them, whereas a safe investor is advised to look at Reliance Industries shares, because Jio Platforms' benefit is expected to reflect in the balance sheet of Reliance Industries and improvement in the O2C margins is expected to benefit RIL. So, a safer play lies with RIL, whereas a theme play lies with JPL."

Decoding the technical chart of Reliance shares, Mahesh M Ojha of KC Securities said, "Reliance Industries shares have a strong base formation at Rs.1,145. The stock has broken out above Rs.1,200 and is now heading towards the short-term target of Rs.1,265. Existing shareholders and fresh buyers can initiate coverage with a strict stop-loss at Rs.1,145 for the targets of Rs.1,265, Rs.1,290 and Rs.1,350 in the short-term horizon."

Speaking on the outlook of Jio Platforms shares, Arun Kejriwal, Founder of Kejriwal Research and Investment Services, said, "The weighted average of Jio Platforms shares improved from Rs.1,360 to Rs.1,410, as the stock hit a new high of Rs.1,489.70 per share during the Thursday session.

My suggestion to Jio Platforms shareholders is to hold the scrip and maintain a strict stop-loss below the listing price of Rs.1,410. The Reliance Group stock may touch the Rs.1,500 and Rs.1,550 levels, as the Jio Platforms Q2 Results 2026 met the market estimates."
